criterion_notes.c1: Although a background section summarizes national household water and sanitation coverage deficits from secondary IBGE (2010, 2012) and Moraes et al. (2011) reports, the study's empirical investigation examines municipal and regional access to federal infrastructure financing ('acesso aos recursos'), not household or community water or sanitation service access.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording: YES — the paper examines federal sanitation public policy, institutional restructuring (Ministry of Cities, Law 11.445/2007, PPP Law 11.079/2004), parliamentary budget amendments, and intergovernmental allocation/credit-eligibility rules for OGU grants and FGTS/FAT loans. Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: NO — the analysis focuses on macro-political/fiscal governance and intergovernmental infrastructure financing rules ('regras de acesso aos recursos', CMN municipal debt limits, FGTS Curatorial Council guidelines) governing municipal/utility borrowing rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community service access. Even under the plain reading of Criterion 2, the paper is still excluded because it lacks an empirical service-access outcome (Criterion 4 = no).
criterion_notes.c3: Contains descriptive empirical analysis of administrative public-finance datasets compiled from Sigplan, Siga Brasil, and FGTS-Caixa / FAT-BNDES records (provided by the Ministry of Cities) covering federal non-onerous and onerous sanitation investments between 2003 and 2010 (with contract-level municipal analyses for 2004–2009).
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4: all empirical outcomes reported in the study are fiscal and intergovernmental financing metrics — federal sanitation budget transfers as a share of GDP, committed vs. disbursed R$ billions, share of parliamentary amendments, and regional/municipal distribution of Caixa (FGTS) and BNDES (FAT) loan contracts across 570 municipalities by population bracket, HDI, and GDP per capita. No household or community water or sanitation access, connection, availability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or service-exclusion outcome is empirically measured.
criterion_notes.c5: The unit of analysis (federal budget actions and Brazilian municipalities contracting federal loans, N=570 in the Caixa/FGTS municipal table), policy/financing context, fiscal/contracting outcomes, and descriptive administrative-data / political-economy study design are clearly identifiable, though situated at the intergovernmental public-finance level rather than household/community service access.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Portuguese (with Portuguese and English abstracts), which is eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

evidence_quotes.quote: Thus, this article aims at studying the recent policy of sanitation in Brazil.

Os financiamentos, via contratos, foram classificados segundo municípios contemplados, considerando as seguintes variáveis: componentes do saneamento básico, regiões, Produto Interno Bruto, Índice de Desenvolvimento Humano, faixa populacional e tipo de prestador dos serviços.
Os critérios de alocação de recursos do FGTS para cada unidade da federação são definidos pelo seu Conselho Curador.

Embora os investimentos do Governo Federal venham se ampliando, os dados sugerem que ainda persiste uma desigualdade do acesso aos recursos não onerosos e onerosos entre as macrorregiões brasileiras. Os pequenos municípios e a região Norte, onde os déficits são maiores, continuam com dificuldades de acesso aos recursos.

Borja (2011) avaliou que diversos fatores contribuem para essa realidade, a saber: falta de capacidade dos pequenos municípios de elaborar projetos e solicitar financiamento; não enquadramento dos municípios nas regras de acesso aos recursos; dificuldades de atender as diretrizes do Conselho Curador do FGTS, que não dialogam com as necessidades do saneamento básico, tanto em termos do público-alvo, como na distribuição dos recursos entre os componentes.

raw_response.exposure: Federal basic sanitation policy and intergovernmental financing mechanisms in Brazil (non-onerous OGU budget allocations, parliamentary amendments, and onerous FGTS-Caixa and FAT-BNDES credit programs and municipal borrowing rules)
raw_response.outcome: Federal budget commitments and disbursements for basic sanitation (in R$ and % of GDP) and distribution of contracted FGTS/FAT infrastructure loans across sanitation components, macro-regions, and municipal population, HDI, and GDP per capita brackets
raw_response.population_and_sample: Federal sanitation budget programs/actions (Sigplan and Siga Brasil, 2003–2010) and Brazilian municipalities receiving federal onerous sanitation loan contracts (FGTS-Caixa and FAT-BNDES, 2004–2009; 570 municipalities in the Caixa/FGTS municipal population table)
raw_response.rationale: Borja (2014) conducts a descriptive quantitative-qualitative analysis of Brazilian federal sanitation policy and public investments (2003–2010), compiling Sigplan, Siga Brasil, FGTS-Caixa, and FAT-BNDES administrative datasets. Although background pages cite national IBGE water and sanitation deficit figures, the empirical analysis measures only intergovernmental financial outcomes — federal budget shares of GDP, committed versus disbursed R$, parliamentary amendment shares, and which municipalities signed FGTS loan contracts ('acesso aos recursos') by region, population size, HDI, and GDP per capita — without measuring any household or community water or sanitation service access, connection, availability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or service-exclusion outcome (E04, Wrong outcome). In addition, while the paper satisfies the plain wording of Criterion 2 by examining federal sanitation governance and intergovernmental credit rules, it fails the narrow 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 reading because macro-fiscal/political governance and municipal loan-eligibility rules govern municipal infrastructure borrowing rather than directly governing household or community service access. Because Criterion 4 is unmet regardless, both decision and plain_criterion2_decision are exclude (E04).
raw_response.study_design: Descriptive quantitative-qualitative administrative-data and policy analysis of federal sanitation expenditures and municipal loan contracts (2003–2010)
